copy.subject: a Kafka cluster
copy.writes: every produce, fetch, topic or config change and offset commit, and every read of a record, a config, a log directory or a consumer group

investigation.classifierDescription: a question about the cluster's topics, partitions, replicas, brokers or offset ranges, such as which topics are under-replicated or offline, how partitions and leaders are spread over brokers, or how far a topic's offsets reach, that is answered from what the run establishes
investigation.objective: Your objective is a question about this Kafka cluster's metadata: its topics, partitions, replicas, brokers and offset ranges. Answer it from what you establish.
investigation.toolDescription: Run one bounded metadata read of a Kafka cluster, written as one JSON object with at most the keys read, topic, after and limit. read is "topics" (each topic's partition count, replication factor and offline and under-replicated partitions), "brokers" (each broker's node id and rack, and the cluster id), "partitions" (one topic's partitions: leader, replicas, in-sync replicas, offline flag) or "offsets" (one topic's partitions: earliest offset, end offset and the span between them); "partitions" and "offsets" need "topic". limit is 1 to 500, default 50, and "after" is the last topic name, node id or partition id of the answer before, to read on. A record's key, value, headers and timestamp, a broker's host and port, configs, log directories and consumer groups are never read. An offset span is how far the offsets reach, not a message count: compaction, transaction markers and retention make the two differ. A request with any other key or read, or a limit past the row budget, is refused rather than answered in part, and you are told why.
investigation.toolRule: Read the cluster with run_read_query, one JSON request at a time: {"read": "topics"}, {"read": "brokers"}, {"read": "partitions", "topic": "orders"} or {"read": "offsets", "topic": "orders"}, each with an optional "limit" and "after" and no other key. Name a topic exactly as the inventory names it. Kafka's internal topics are never read. Answers carry names, counts and offsets only: a record's key, value, headers and timestamp, a broker's host and port, configs, log directories and consumer groups are withheld, so what this run establishes is the cluster's topics, partitions, replicas, brokers and offset ranges, never what a record says or who consumes it. An offset span is how far a partition's offsets reach, not how many records it holds: compaction, transaction markers and retention make the two differ, so never report a span as a message count. A read whose answer says more follow is a page: read on with "after" set to the last topic, node id or partition of the answer. Report what the evidence supports, and nothing further.

qualifier: s per read, over a client that holds only Metadata and ListOffsets
posture.title: Agent mode reads Kafka's topics, partitions, brokers and offsets, over a client that holds only two reads
body: Agent mode runs Kafka metadata reads it wrote itself, each one JSON request for the topic list, the broker list, one topic's partitions or one topic's earliest and end offsets, and answers names, counts and offsets only: topic names, partition and replica counts, leader and replica node ids, broker node ids and racks and the cluster id, never a record's key, value, headers or timestamp, a broker's host and port, a config, a log directory or a consumer group, bounded to

seconds each and refused past them rather than cut. An offset span is reported as a span, never as a message count. Studio's agent client holds only the Metadata request, sent with topic auto-creation off, and the ListOffsets request at the earliest and latest offsets, so it cannot fetch, produce, create or delete a topic, commit an offset or change a config, and it never names an internal topic. Nothing reaches your editor.
posture.handover: A Kafka answer is never run in your editor: the hand-over is not offered on this engine, so the run produces its answer on its own read-only path only.

grounding.omissionAdvice: A topic is listed to agent mode by its partitions and offsets only. Read any topic with run_read_query, for example {"read": "offsets", "topic": "orders"} for each partition's earliest and end offsets of the topic orders.

text.title: Run a read-only Kafka metadata read
description: Run one read-only Kafka metadata read on a connection: one JSON object as text, {"read": "topics"} for the topics with their partition and replica counts, {"read": "brokers"} for broker node ids and racks, {"read": "partitions", "topic": "orders"} for one topic's partitions with their leader and replicas, or {"read": "offsets", "topic": "orders"} for each partition's earliest and end offsets; each also takes "limit" (1 to 500, default 50) and "after", the last topic name, node id or partition id read, to read on. Metadata only: no record's key, value, headers or timestamp is ever fetched, a broker's host and port, configs, log directories and consumer groups are not read, Kafka's internal topics and a platform's own topics (a leading underscore, or connect-) are withheld, and an offset span is not a message count. Any other request is refused before the broker is reached. Runs on

; this tool takes no offset, so page inside the request with "limit" and "after": an answer that holds as many rows as its "limit" may have more after it, so read on with "after" until an answer holds fewer.
text.fewerFields: A Kafka read's columns are fixed, so none can be left out
readPast: rows returned, set "after" to the last topic name, node id or partition id among them.
text.rowOverCap: One row of this result is larger than the 32 KiB result limit. Read a narrower listing, one topic's partitions or offsets, and run it again.
